title: Overdub II: RPG Maker MZ Default Event Sounds and Background Loops
shortText: The 208 RPG Maker MZ default sound effects Overdub left, plus all 29 BGS loops, voiced again under the same names.
html:
The rest of RPG Maker MZ's default sounds, in Overdub's voice

208 sound effects and 29 background loops, named exactly like the MZ defaults they replace: every default sound effect Overdub left playing, and every default background sound.

What it replaces

A new RPG Maker MZ project ships 345 sound effects and 29 background sounds. Overdub replaced the 137 sound effects the default database plays. This pack covers everything else: the 208 names you pick yourself in Play SE (doors, chests, switches, footsteps, monsters, animals, bells, machines and the alternate battle and spell takes) and all 29 Play BGS loops (rain, wind, fire, river, sea, storm, city, night and the rest).

Copy ogg/se over your project's audio/se and ogg/bgs over audio/bgs, after a backup. Your events keep their volumes, pitches and pans and play these instead. No event edits, no plugin. With both packs, all 345 default sound effect names in a new project play new sounds.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Ship it in as many games as you like, deployed with or without MZ's encryption. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Every sound is synthesised from code: no audio from RPG Maker or any other source was used, only the file names match.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: the whole doors, chests and mechanisms family (33 sound effects) and two background loops (Rain2 and Fire2), copied unaltered from the paid files and laid out the same way, so you can drop it into a test project and try it in your own events.

One game, one sound

Overdub II is built in Overdub's identity, lantern bronze and glass in a stone hall: the same two struck materials, the same stone and timber floor, the same hall. A door, a wolf and Overdub's sword cut sound like they belong to one game, which is the point of replacing the defaults at all.

Tested in MZ's own engine code

  • MZ's runtime scripts played every sound effect the way Play SE does: 208 of 208 decoded, and 208 of 208 again on the engine's own Vorbis decoder (the path Safari and iOS players take).
  • Every background sound played through Play BGS: 29 of 29, and for each one the engine read the loop tags in the file and looped the whole file.
  • With Overdub's files in the same folder, all 345 default sound effect names played. An encrypted deployment passed too.
  • Each sound runs about as long as the default it replaces (median ratio x0.927; 201 of 208 within x0.5 to x1.6), so a Wait you timed to the old sound still fits.

Fit

  • OGG for the engine and WAV originals, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, under the exact default names.
  • 29 seamless loops with the LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags MZ reads, and the same loop as a sampler loop in every background WAV.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 0.68 dB, so the default volume of 90 works for all of them.
  • A manifest naming every file with what it is, its length beside the default's, and its brightness, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 2170 checks, 0 failed.

Already own Overdub?

Every file here was measured against every Overdub file (32469 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 32469 of 32469 are separate sounds. No name is in both packs. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

RPG Maker MZ only: MV uses some different default names and plays m4a files on phones, and this pack was tested in MZ's engine code only. The animals and creatures are stylised calls in the pack's identity, not recordings of animals. The 27 music effects are music and are not included. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The store graphics are made by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by the makers of RPG Maker. RPG Maker is a trademark of its owner.
